## Proportional-hazard distortion {#sec-recipe-distortions-ph-distortion}

You want to load expected loss into a price in a way that charges more for the
tail than for the body, and you want the loading to be a *property of the
measure* rather than a judgement applied case by case.

```{python}
import numpy as np
g = build('''distortion PHDistortion ph 0.7''')
s = np.linspace(0, 1, 11)
qd(pd.DataFrame({'s': s, 'g(s)': g.g(s)}).set_index('s'))
```

The curve is the clearer statement of the same thing -- it bows above the
diagonal everywhere, which *is* the loading:

```{python}
#| fig-cap: "PH distortion, rho = 0.7. Above the diagonal is the load."
g.plot()
```

The proportional-hazard distortion is `g(s) = s**rho` with `rho = 0.7 < 1`.
Applied to the survival function, it stretches small exceedance probabilities
upward -- a 1-in-100 event is priced as though it were more likely than it is --
and leaves certainty alone.

Concavity is what makes it a coherent risk measure: the premium it produces is
subadditive, so combining two books never costs more than pricing them apart.
`rho = 1` is the identity (pure expected loss, no load); smaller `rho` loads
more heavily.

::: {.callout-note collapse="true" title="The check"}

```{python}
# a distortion is a probability-to-probability map: g(0)=0, g(1)=1
assert abs(g.g(0.0)) < 1e-12
assert abs(g.g(1.0) - 1.0) < 1e-12
# increasing, and CONCAVE (the coherence property)
s = np.linspace(0, 1, 201)
gs = g.g(s)
assert np.all(np.diff(gs) >= -1e-12)
assert np.all(np.diff(gs, 2) <= 1e-9)
# a load, never a discount: g(s) >= s everywhere
assert np.all(gs >= s - 1e-12)
```

:::
